en: Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, known locally as the monkey-eating eagle, is the national bird and is critically endangered due to deforestation.
The Supreme Court is the highest court in the Philippines and holds the judicial power to interpret the Constitution.
The indigenous Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains of the Cordilleras over two thousand years ago.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the two-way radiotelephone and discovered the physical law of electrical kinetic resistance.
The sampaguita, a fragrant white jasmine flower, was officially declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1936.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
Filipino, the national language, is primarily based on Tagalog and incorporates words from other native Philippine and foreign languages.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño with a rhythmic two-steps forward, one-step backward dance.
The Bill of Rights in Article III of the 1987 Philippine Constitution protects citizens against government abuse.
Filipino painter Juan Luna won a gold medal at the 1884 Madrid Exposition for his Spoliarium painting.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is traditionally shown when a community helps a family physically relocate their nipa hut.
